service.description: A step of a template tree (rootWorkEffortId, a WorkEffort with isTemplate Y and a process policy in effect): new (workEffortName; under parentWorkEffortId, a node of the same tree, else the root) or changed (workEffortId), with its step policy from now (isRequired, roleTypeId, dueOffsetDays; a change ends the policy in effect and starts the next), and the steps of the same tree it waits for (dependsOnIds; a cycle or another tree's step is refused, DEPENDENCY_INVALID). With end, the step's policy ends now: the step is left out of new executions. Needs the permission of the policy using the process (PERMISSION_DENIED; PROCESS_UNAVAILABLE for a template with no policy in effect). A maintenance procedure (impl-maintenance P6) takes its checked path: WORK_PROCESS_EDIT in its organization, not retired (PROCESS_RETIRED), an approved one back to Draft, and the step's response policy (responseKindEnumId, measurementTypeId, measurementUomId, minimumValue, maximumValue, evidenceRequired, commentRequired, waiverAllowed; VALUE_INVALID).

parameter.name: purposeEnumId
parameter.description: A new step's purpose; the root's when empty

service.description: A template (templateWorkEffortId: isTemplate Y, its process policy in effect) made into fresh work by the two-pass copy of design-maintenance §4.2: the root and each step whose policy is in effect (an ended step left out with its sub-steps) copied with their definition fields only (the template flag, status, resolution, actual dates, effort and recurrence reset; due dates from each step's offset after startDate, now when empty), the WeatDependsOn edges inside the tree remapped, one WeatBasedOn association from each new node to its template node, the step and process policies copied, and each step assigned (Assignee) to the party roleParties names for its role (a role named for no one stays a requirement). rootFields override the root's workEffortName, description and ownerPartyId. One tree in the caller's transaction; a retry with operationKey answers the first root (repeated). Needs the permission of the policy using the process. A maintenance procedure takes its checked path (impl-maintenance P6, design §4.2 step 1): MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE in its organization; approved (PROCESS_NOT_APPROVED, PROCESS_RETIRED), effective now (PROCESS_NOT_EFFECTIVE) and applicable to assetId or facilityId (PROCESS_NOT_APPLICABLE); then the copy, and each template node's requirements copied to its new node (F58).

parameter.name: assetId
parameter.description: A procedure's target, for its applicability

parameter.name: idMap
parameter.description: Each template node's id to its new node's

service.description: The managed-work rule (impl-people §4, impl-maintenance §4, in the same words): the generic task and work-effort services refuse a root that has a MaintenanceWorkOrder row and its steps, and work whose process policy guards execution (MANAGED_WORK): its own policy, its root's or its parent's. People's checklist tasks stay ordinary tasks (People's policy does not guard). A data check, for any caller; reads nothing else.

The maintenance procedures of the caller's scope (WORK_PROCESS_VIEW): text (id or name), organization, state (draft, approved, retired; every state when empty), maintenance type, equipment model, effectiveDate (in effect then). With usable (also for MAINTENANCE_PLAN or _SUPERVISE): approved, in effect now and applicable to assetId or facilityId, the procedures new work may use. Never an execution. Each row: name, organization, state, approval, effective dates, applicability, step and required step counts.

A maintenance procedure as its reader sees it (WORK_PROCESS_VIEW in its organization; a technician assigned to work made of it reads it read only): the header (name, organization, state, estimate, applicability, effective dates, approval and last author), the steps in order with their depth, group flag, response policy, dependencies, requirements and instruction summary, the requirements, the current instructions (an author's draft, else the published one), the approval history (WorkEffortApproval), the findings that block publication, and what the caller may do (edit, request approval, approve or why not, retire, use for new work).

A new maintenance procedure, a draft of organizationPartyId (WORK_PROCESS_EDIT in it; the caller's one organization when empty): a template root (WetTask, WepMaintenance, the WorkEffortProcedure flow) with its process policy (WppMaintenanceProcedure, guarding execution) and applicability; cloned from sourceWorkEffortId (a procedure the caller reads) with new ids, its steps, dependencies, requirements and instruction texts as drafts and no approval. Or a change of one (workEffortId): its name, description, estimated hours and applicability; an approved one goes back to Draft (PROCESS_RETIRED for a retired one).
A step of a procedure one place up or down among its siblings (WORK_PROCESS_EDIT; the keyboard and terminal reorder). moved false at either end.
The steps of the same procedure a step waits for (WeatDependsOn; dependsOnIds replaces them): a step of another procedure or a loop is refused (DEPENDENCY_INVALID). WORK_PROCESS_EDIT.

One planned requirement of a procedure's step (or its root), new, changed or removed (remove): kind product (a part, WorkEffortProduct of type consume, dated: a change ends the row and starts the next; productId, estimatedQuantity), asset (equipment needed, WorkEffortAssetNeeded; assetProductId, estimatedQuantity, estimatedDuration) or skill (WorkEffortSkillStandard; skillTypeEnumId, estimatedNumPeople, estimatedDuration; People's minimumSkillLevel joins in Maintenance's P8, impl-maintenance F75). WORK_PROCESS_EDIT.

A procedure step's (or its root's) draft instruction text (WorkEffortContent WectProcedureDraft; a new draft ends the one before); with end, no instruction from the next approval. The next approval publishes it as a WectInstruction row (impl-maintenance F68). WORK_PROCESS_EDIT.

The instruction of a procedure node in effect now (a reader of the procedure), or of an execution's node (a work order's root or step the caller reads as Maintenance does): its template node's instruction in effect when the execution was made, through its WeatBasedOn link; nothing is copied, so a later approval does not change it.

A draft procedure put for approval (WORK_PROCESS_EDIT or _APPROVE in its organization): its definition is checked first (PUBLICATION_INVALID naming each finding: a group with a response, a reading with no measurement or unit, a unit of another kind, bounds the wrong way round, a dependency outside the procedure or in a loop, no step); a WorkEffortApproval row is requested (impl-maintenance F44) and the organization's approvers (WORK_PROCESS_APPROVE, not the last author unless self-approval is allowed) are told on WorkProcessApproval. A request waiting is answered (repeated).

The approval of a draft waiting for it (WORK_PROCESS_APPROVE in its organization), from ProcedureDetail or as the WorkProcessApproval topic's approve service (recordId; the framework's approve#NotificationMessage calls it as the user deciding): not by the last author unless the organization's MaintenancePolicy allows self-approval (SELF_APPROVAL); APPROVAL_NOT_REQUESTED when none waits, PUBLICATION_INVALID with findings. The decision on its WorkEffortApproval row, the procedure Approved from effectiveDate (now or later; DATE_PAST), each changed draft instruction published as a WectInstruction row (F68), the definition stored as a PDF (WectPublishedProcedure) and the notices read.

The refusal of a draft waiting for approval, with the reason (WORK_PROCESS_APPROVE in its organization; the WorkProcessApproval topic's refuse service): the request refused, the procedure still a draft.
A procedure retired (WORK_PROCESS_APPROVE in its organization): no new work is made of it from now; a request waiting is cancelled; its executions and history stay, and it stays searchable.

The work made of a procedure that the caller's maintenance scope covers (WORK_PROCESS_VIEW): each work order's id, name, target, when it was made, state and outcome, newest first; openable for a reader of work.

Whether a procedure may be named for an equipment model (productId: Product360's maintenance default, an owner contract with Products), equipment (assetId) or a facility (facilityId): a maintenance procedure, not retired, whose applicability admits it. A data check (reasonCode PROCESS_UNAVAILABLE, PROCESS_RETIRED, PROCESS_NOT_APPLICABLE); the caller checks its own permission.

A work order's checklist for a reader of it (MAINTENANCE_VIEW in its organization, or its assigned technician): each step in order with its depth, group flag, state, policy (required, response kind, reading and bounds, evidence, comment, waiver), blockers (the dependencies not done), assignees, instruction, current check (outcome, reading, findings, notes, evidence), failures and waiver, and what the caller may do (start, respond, skip, waive, correct); the checks newest first, the waivers and the amendments; the next actionable step, the required steps open (the gate of the work order's Complete) and the stored completed checklist. workEffortId is the root or one of its steps.

A step of a work order in progress (STATUS_INVALID otherwise), by its assigned technician (MAINTENANCE_EXECUTE, assigned to the step or its root; NOT_ASSIGNED) or a supervisor; a leaf (GROUP_NO_RESPONSE), its dependencies and its groups' done (DEPENDENCY_OPEN). action start: the step in progress. action skip: an optional step (SKIP_NOT_ALLOWED) cancelled with the reason (comments; REASON_REQUIRED). action respond (design §4.3): outcome (pass or fail) for a pass or fail step (OUTCOME_REQUIRED), measurementValue (VALUE_REQUIRED) and measurementUomId for a reading, observedDate (now when empty; DATE_FUTURE), comments, evidence (evidenceContentIds, files of the work order; contentFile, files uploaded with it, stored on the root named for the step; voiceFile, a voice note), supersededCheckId and correctionReason for a correction of a check (REASON_REQUIRED), operationKey (a retry answers the first check; changed input OPERATION_KEY_CONFLICT). The policy, bounds, organization and actor are the execution's and the caller's, never given. A missing file or comment, a wrong unit, an out-of-range reading or a failure is saved as an unresolved check (its findings) and leaves the step open; an accepted check completes it. A reading is a Measurement of the step; a counter reading also goes through MaintenanceResourceServices.record#MaintenanceMeter with the Measurement linked. A step's response is never a group's: groups follow their steps.

The voice note of a check (its recorder or a supervisor) as text, through SpeechServices.transcribe#Audio, added to the check's transcript, only when the work order's organization turns transcription on (MaintenancePolicy voiceNoteTranscription, off by default; otherwise reasonCode TRANSCRIPTION_OFF and nothing is sent). A transcription that does not work is an answer (reasonCode); the audio stays the evidence either way. Called in a transaction of its own after record#ProcessStep.

A supervisor's waiver of a step (MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE in its organization; a technician is refused, PERMISSION_DENIED) while the work is in progress or held: a leaf not done (STEP_DONE) whose execution policy allows it (WAIVER_NOT_ALLOWED), with the reason (REASON_REQUIRED). The step is complete; the failed check it answers (workEffortCheckId, else the step's latest unresolved one) stays.

A supervisor's change of an open work order's execution (MAINTENANCE_SUPERVISE; completed, closed or cancelled work is corrected, not amended, WORK_CLOSED). Each change of changeList has an action (the user's call of Nov 12, P7 review): add (workEffortName, parentWorkEffortId the root or a group, GROUP_REQUIRED otherwise, sequenceNum, description, estimatedWorkTime, the policy fields, dependsOnIds: a new step not started; a complete group it joins reopens, named among the invalidations); remove (workEffortId: a step, or a group with its steps, not yet started and with no check, STEP_STARTED otherwise; it is cancelled and named in the amendment, and what waited for it no longer does); or change (the default): it names steps of it and their new step policy fields (isRequired, responseKindEnumId, measurementTypeId, measurementUomId, minimumValue, maximumValue, evidenceRequired, commentRequired, waiverAllowed) or dependencies (dependsOnIds, steps of the same tree, no loop: DEPENDENCY_INVALID). With preview, the changes, the acceptances they invalidate (a complete step whose requirement changed, or that now waits for work not done) and the findings (complete steps waiting for a reopened one), and nothing written. Else, with the reason (REASON_REQUIRED): the step policies from now, the dependencies, the amendment record, and each invalidated step back in progress with its accepted checks invalidated and its waiver ended (both kept). operationKey: a retry answers the first.
A work order's completed checklist and exception record as a PDF (a reader of it; design §12): the one stored at close (contentLocation), else made now (pdfBytes). No cost.

The evidence policy of a work effort's files (RecordFiles' get#ContentType, impl-maintenance F69): for managed work, whether files may be added or changed (not on closed or cancelled work; a procedure's are its authors') and the files a check names as evidence or the stored checklist, which are never removed, replaced or given a new version; ordinary work answers managed false. A data check; the caller checks who reads the record.
A work effort's file a check names as evidence is not changed (EVIDENCE_PROTECTED): update#WorkEffortContent calls it. A data check.
